slash.tradingProfileHelp: Show or update your investor profile.
slash.tradingProfileUsage:
Usage
/profile show
/profile set <field> <value>
/profile enable|disable <segment>
/profile reset

Examples
/profile set risk-level balanced
/profile set reserve-pct-nav 0.2
/profile set segment-target crypto 0.1

Fractions: 0.2 means 20%.
Segments: {segments}

Risk appetite
risk-level: one setting for all of it -
conservative, balanced or aggressive. It also
sets the limits below.
risk-capacity: how much loss you can afford.
risk-willingness: how much loss you are
comfortable with.
These two take the same three levels, but not
in the same write as risk-level.

Horizon and goal
horizon <segment> <short|long>: hold each segment
for the short or the long term.
goal <{goals}>: preserve capital,
steady income or growth.
preferred-locale: language of the scheduled
runs (vi or en).

Buying limits (share of your total assets)
reserve-pct-nav: cash you always keep.
risk-per-trade-pct-nav: most you may lose if one
new buy hits its stop-loss.
maximum-open-risk-pct-nav: most you may lose if
every holding hits its stop-loss together.
maximum-sector-pct-nav: most you may put in one
sector.
regime-scale: most of the amount you plan to buy
that is used each time (0.75 uses 75%). A
defensive market can lower it further.

Buying and selling in steps
entry-tranche-pct is how much of a new buy goes in
first (0.5 = half now, half once the plan holds).
take-profit-tranche-pct is how much you sell at the
first target; the rest keeps running with a
stop-loss that only moves up.
Both take 0.2 to 1.

Target or cap - which one you want
segment-target <segment> <fraction>: the share of
your book a segment is steered towards. Set it
and the other segments give up their share of
the difference, so the targets still total 100%.
This is the one that moves money. Your cash
reserve is never touched, and a target that would
eat into it is refused.
A target you set is kept: changing risk-level or
turning a segment on or off recalculates everything
around it rather than over it. reset clears it,
and so does turning that segment off.

segment-cap <segment> <fraction>: the most of your
book a segment may reach.
position-cap <segment> <fraction>: the most any one
stock or coin in the segment may take.
A cap is only room: raising one lets a buy fill
further, it moves nothing there.
Lowering segment-cap pulls the limits under it down
with it, and is refused below the segment's target.
A segment you turned off takes neither.

What turning a segment off does
Its limits close: nothing in that segment is sized
or bought.
The remaining segments' targets are recalculated as
if it had never existed; turning it back on
recalculates them again with it.
risk-level recalculates every limit but keeps the
segments you turned off.
reset goes back to the default segments and keeps
your watchlist.

slash.tradingTradeUsage:
Placing an order
/trade spot <[venue:]ticker> buy|sell <quantity> [limit <price>] [tp <price>] [sl <price>]

Setting or moving an exit
/trade exit <[venue:]ticker> [qty <quantity>] [tp <price>] [sl <price>]

After it is staged
/trade confirm [token]
/trade cancel <[venue:]ticker>
/trade reconcile [token]

Switching buying off and on
/trade halt
/trade resume

Example
/trade spot BTC buy 0.01 sl 90000

tp is the take-profit price and sl the stop-loss
price. limit waits for that price; leave it out to
trade at the market price.
On a plan that sells part at its target and
trails the rest, set only sl - a tp would sell
everything there.
Write venue:ticker, such as okx:BTC or binance:BTC, only
where more than one venue could fill it.
slash.tradingTradeUnknownToken: That token has expired, been used, or was never issued. Stage the order again and confirm the new one.
slash.tradingTradeExitCancelled: The resting exit on {ticker} is gone. The position is open with nothing guarding it.
slash.tradingTradeNoExit: There is no resting exit on {ticker} to cancel.
slash.tradingTradeNothingOutstanding: Nothing staged, no exit placed through OpenAlpha, and nothing the exchange took that your book is missing.
slash.tradingTradeNoStaged: There is no order waiting for confirmation. Stage one with /trade spot first.
slash.tradingTradeManyStaged: More than one order is waiting, so name the one you mean: /trade confirm <token>. Run /trade to see them.
slash.tradingTradeNothingUnmirrored: Every order that reached the exchange is in your book. Nothing to reconcile.
slash.tradingTradeReconciled: Settled. That order has stopped counting against your caps.
slash.tradingTradeAutoSettledOne: Your book has caught up on {count} order, so it no longer counts against your caps. Nothing else is outstanding.
slash.tradingTradeAutoSettled: Your book has caught up on {count} orders, so they no longer count against your caps. Nothing else is outstanding.
slash.tradingTradeUnknownIntent: No outstanding order carries that token. Run /trade reconcile to see what is still open.
slash.tradingTradeFailed: The order did not go out: {reason}
slash.tradingTradeHalted: Buying is off. No new buy goes out until you run /trade resume, and that holds through a restart. Sells, exits and cancels still work, and every resting stop stays exactly where it is.
slash.tradingTradeResumed: Buying is back on. Orders still go through your caps and your confirmation, same as before.

errors.profileOutOfBounds: {field} must be between {minimum} and {maximum}. Write it as a fraction: 0.2 is 20%.
